plan.notes: Source: The University of Tampa 'Four-Year Degree Plan for Major in Psychology, B.A.' (official sample plan PDF, https://ut.smartcatalogiq.com/-/media/institution/ut/csme/psychology/FourYear%20Degree%20Plan%20for%20Major%20in%20Psychology%20BA.pdf), transcribed term by term from the university's current online catalog (Catalog 2026-2027; the plan PDF itself does not print a catalog year). The plan is explicitly a SAMPLE four-year plan ('Note that this is a sample four-year plan...'). Course codes/titles/credits taken verbatim; prereq arrays are empty (the plan does not publish per-course prerequisites; not invented). 'PSY 200/300/400+ level — Satisfy emphasis requirements as needed' slots are the catalog's own category rows; the specific qualifying PSY course is chosen per the catalog. 'Humanities / Fine Arts or Social Science (Bacc. Exp.)' and 'Natural Science (Bacc. Exp.)' are Baccalaureate Experience general-education category slots. Junior Fall and Junior Spring show catalog 'and/or' ranges (12-16 and 13-17) on a 'PSY 312 and/or PSY 300+' row in each semester: PSY 312 is a single 4cr requirement, placed in Junior Fall (it may instead be taken in Spring, swapping the semesters' PSY slots); the Junior Spring PSY slot is therefore the 'and/or' PSY 300+ emphasis option. this seed resolves both semesters at the MINIMUM (PSY 312 only) per the range rule — a student taking the optional PSY 300+ course in either or both semesters reaches up to 16/17. Minimum-path total is 123 credits; the degree requires a minimum of 124 credit hours (plan notes), reachable via the optional 'and/or' courses and/or electives. Catalog notes carried over: PSY 211 must be completed with a grade of 'C' or better after taking MAT 160 (or higher); PSY 312 must be completed before enrolling in most 400-level courses; minimum 2.0 GPA overall and in the major; minimum 24 hours in psychology including 20 hours of 300-400 level courses (at least one 400-level). No TCCNS in Florida; transfer_confidence is empty.
